blocks.title: Sequence diagram
blocks.text: Sequence diagrams show how objects in a system interact with each other in a particular order. They help in understanding the flow of messages between objects over time.

Figure 1.11 continues the room example. The user and three boxes (toys box, books box and clothes box) each have a vertical lifeline. The messages, read from top to bottom, are: open() each box; put the toys, books and clothes inside their boxes; then close() each box.

blocks.alt: Top left: a sequence diagram with lifelines for the user and three boxes and messages open, put inside and close in time order. Top right: an activity diagram from start through order placement and food preparation to a ready decision leading to delivery or re-preparation, then end. Bottom left: unit, integration, system and acceptance testing as widening layers. Bottom right: kinds of development tools with examples.
blocks.caption: Sequence and activity diagrams, the levels of testing and development tools (original diagram after Figures 1.11 and 1.12 and topics 1.7 and 1.8).
blocks.long_description: A sequence diagram gives each object a vertical lifeline and draws the messages between them as arrows in time order from top to bottom: the user opens each box, puts the toys, books and clothes inside, and closes each box. An activity diagram shows the flow of a process from a start node through steps and decisions to an end node: an order is placed, the food is prepared, and if it is ready it is delivered, otherwise it is prepared again. Testing goes from single units to their integration, the whole system and finally acceptance by users. Development tools include editors, translators, compilers, debuggers, integrated development environments, computing platforms and code repositories.
